skillSays: Write focused, reusable Playwright scripts and run them through the skill's run.js executor (or inline with -e), instead of ad-hoc one-liners
Detect running dev servers first with helpers.detectDevServers(); use the only result automatically, ask when there are several or none
Prefer user-facing locators in order: getByRole with a name, getByLabel, getByText, getByTestId; rely on auto-waiting, not sleeps or networkidle
Report actions, failures and artifact paths, and never claim success without checking the resulting page
Visible browser by default, headless only when asked or when there is no display; PW_* env vars control headless, channel, artifact and script dirs
Run `npm run setup` once to install Playwright and Chromium

changes: Wrote one script with getByLabel/getByRole locators that reads the resulting DOM after each submit, so the report states what the page actually showed for the invalid and valid cases
Listened to page requests during the flow and found the 'account created' success never hits a server
Used the inline -e mode for a quick probe and confirmed the email is injected with innerHTML (an payload really executed)
Flagged that detectDevServers() returned the macOS AirPlay listener on :5000 instead of the app, and used the known URL
Attached console, pageerror, request and response listeners before the first click, so the TypeError was captured at the moment it happened
Compared clicking Book with and without selecting a slot first, which isolates the cause (selected is undefined until a slot click)
Confirmed the server side saw exactly one POST, only in the second scenario
Noticed the success banner appears even when the response is a 501 (res.ok is never checked)
